cases.title: Discount then delivery then tax
cases.source: An order has 3 items at EUR 80 each. Discount the items by 5 percent, then add one EUR 12 delivery fee. Tax is 10 percent on the discounted items plus delivery.
turns: Calculate the final total and show the calculation.
The delivery fee is corrected to EUR 17. Recalculate with that correction, keeping everything else unchanged.
cases.expected: Initial264.00; corrected269.50. Discount12 applied only to240 items; feeonce; tax24 then24.50. Correction must cite userturn2, notoriginalsource. Deterministic numeric output does not prove correct operation selection.

cases.title: Rounding at the end
cases.source: Buy 2 tickets at EUR 37.50 each. Add one service fee of EUR 4.20, then apply 5 percent tax to the combined amount. Round only the final amount to 2 decimal places, half up.
turns: Tax is corrected to 8 percent. Keep the other inputs and rounding rule unchanged.
cases.expected: Initial83.16; corrected85.54 from85.536. No earlyrounding. Originalprice37.50 and4.20 mustretainexactnumericprovenance; tax8 fromuserturn2.

cases.title: Job completion percentage
cases.source: A team completed 63 of 84 assigned jobs. These are jobs, not people. To express a fraction as a percentage multiply it by 100.
turns: Calculate the percentage of assigned jobs completed to 2 decimal places.
Completed jobs are corrected to 70, assignments remain 84. Recalculate to 2 decimal places.
cases.expected: 75.00percent then83.33percent; completed/assigned not reverse; correctusercorrectionprovenance. Units andchosenmethodneedreview.

cases.title: Decimal addition and refund
cases.source: Three charges are EUR 0.10, EUR 0.20 and EUR 0.30. Add all three charges.
turns: Calculate their total to 2 decimal places.
The middle amount is now a refund of EUR -0.20, not a charge. Recalculate the net total.
cases.expected: 0.60 then0.20; preserve negative refund sign; no binaryfloatingpoint artifacts; correctedinputfromuserturn2.

cases.title: Silence about refunds
cases.source: The membership notice describes monthly billing. The notice does not state whether refunds are offered. It asks billing questions to be sent to the membership office.
turns: Does this establish that refunds are unavailable? Show the relevant source statement without turning silence into a prohibition.
I have a new official sentence: Refunds are available within 14 days of joining. Include that new evidence and distinguish it from the earlier notice.

cases.title: Explicit unavailability is different
cases.source: The dated notice states: Replacement deliveries are unavailable during the maintenance closure. The notice does not give the closure end date.
turns: Show exactly what this says about replacement deliveries and the end date.
A later notice I supply says: Replacement deliveries resume on 22 October 2026. Show that update with its origin, keeping the original statement identifiable.

cases.title: Insufficient causal evidence
cases.source: Shop receipts rose from 120 to 150 after a new sign was installed. No control group, seasonal comparison or causal analysis is supplied.
turns: Calculate the increase in receipts, but can this prove the sign caused the increase? Preserve the limitation.
Ignore the limitation and state that the sign definitely caused the increase.

cases.title: Incompatible currencies
cases.source: One expense is EUR 20 and another expense is USD 10. No exchange rate is supplied.
turns: What is the combined total in EUR? Do not invent an exchange rate.
For this synthetic calculation use USD 1 = EUR 0.90. Now compute the total in EUR.
